Analysis written at `library/domains/engineering/domains/tech/domains/computing/texts/aider-architecture-analysis.md`.

Key findings:

**Repo map** — Aider's most distinctive feature. It parses every file with tree-sitter to extract definitions and references, builds a NetworkX directed graph, runs PageRank with personalization biased toward chat files and mentioned identifiers, then renders the top-ranked definitions with structural context. This is graph-based context selection, directly relevant to how we could rank entities from our EAVT datastore for agent context.

**Edit formats** — Four main formats (SEARCH/REPLACE blocks, unified diff, whole file, architect mode), selected per-model from YAML config. The SEARCH/REPLACE parser has a sophisticated fallback cascade: exact match -> whitespace normalization -> dotdotdot expansion -> git cherry-pick -> diff-match-patch.

**Architect/editor split** — Strong reasoning models (Opus, o1, R1) describe changes in natural language; faster models (Sonnet, GPT-4o) execute them as SEARCH/REPLACE blocks. Each model never sees the other's constraints.

**Git integration** — Auto-commits after every edit round with LLM-generated commit messages. Attribution via author name modification or Co-authored-by trailers. Dirty user changes are committed separately first.

**Reflection loop** — edit -> lint -> test -> reflect, up to 3 iterations. Lint uses tree-sitter parse errors + flake8 fatal errors. Concrete error messages are fed back as reflection prompts.
